bundle.guidance:
# Incident Post-mortem

The written record of one incident, for SREs and the people who will be on
call next time. It is blameless, chronological and specific. Its only success
criterion is that a reader who was asleep during the incident can reconstruct
it and act on the follow-ups.

## Principles

1. **Timeline before analysis.** The reader needs to know what happened, in
   order, with timestamps, before any interpretation.
2. **Blameless and precise.** Name systems, roles and decisions — never
   individuals as causes. "The deploy gate allowed…", not "X pushed…".
3. **Every follow-up has an owner and a link.** An action item without a
   ticket is a wish.

## Layout grid

Single column at `max-width: 50rem`. The summary block sits at the very top:
severity, duration, impact, status. Then the timeline, then analysis, then the
follow-up table. `--space-xl` between those four blocks and `--space-lg`
inside them. Never reorder: the structure is the contract.

## Typography

Inter throughout at `--size-body`, compact `--line-body`. Timestamps,
identifiers, service names, commands and error strings are always monospace so
they can be grepped out of a paste. Headings stay small — this is a record,
not an essay.

## Colour usage

Red / amber / green come from the `--severity-*` and `--color-status-*`
tokens and mean exactly one thing each: sev1 red (outage or data loss), sev2
amber (major degradation with a workaround), sev3 green (minor or internal).
Use them on badges and the status column only. The red accent must never
appear as decoration — in this design system red always means severity.

## Charts

Chart.js. One chart at most: the impact metric (error rate, latency, failed
jobs) over the incident window, with vertical annotations for detection,
mitigation and resolution. Line only, one or two series, axis in the same
timezone as the timeline — and say which timezone.

## Diagrams

Mermaid `sequenceDiagram` for the failure path across services, and
`flowchart TD` for the detection and escalation path. Keep to the components
that actually participated; a full architecture diagram hides the failure.

## Components and when to use each

- `incident-summary` — the header block: severity badge, duration, impact,
  current status. Required, first, exactly once.
- `severity-badge` — inline severity marker, in the summary and in any list of
  incidents.
- `timeline` — the ordered event list with timestamps. Required. One event per
  entry, each with who or what observed it.
- `impact-table` — affected services, customers, data, and whether the effect
  was recoverable.
- `action-items` — follow-ups with owner, ticket and due date. Required, last.

## Do / don't

- **Do** use absolute UTC timestamps, and state the timezone once at the top.
- **Do** record what was *tried and did not work*; that is the most reusable
  part of a post-mortem.
- **Do** separate contributing factors from the trigger.
- **Don't** write "human error" as a root cause.
- **Don't** publish without every action item having an owner and a ticket.
- **Don't** use red anywhere it does not mean severity.
